confidence_notes: I estimated the restaurant meals, coffee and beer from four standard web searches. Those searches showed crowdsourced cost-of-living aggregates (CityCost Oct 2026, MyLifeElsewhere, Jobicy May 2026, Traveltables Jul 2023, Expatistan), but I only saw search summaries and did not open the pages. Cappuccino prices were consistent at about MX$55–66 (about US$3.0–3.7). Domestic beer was about US$2.0–2.5 per pint in the aggregates. I raised it slightly because the anchor is a restaurant draft serving. Inexpensive meals varied widely, from US$4–6 for a comida corrida to about US$11 for a budget restaurant meal, so I chose a midpoint. Mid-range dinner for two also varied: CityCost gave about US$64 (range US$36–84), while other sources were lower, so I used a figure between them. I found no aggregated Querétaro price for cocktails or glasses of wine. I estimated cocktails at about 2.5x the beer price, which is typical for Mexican cities, and checked this against a good-quality bottle at about MX$337 (Expatistan). The searches mentioned high-end cocktail bars but gave no prices. I did not search for accommodation prices. The four accommodation anchors are my own estimates for a mid-sized, affluent business and colonial-tourism city with limited hostel supply, so they are the least certain. July is not a strong peak season, but business-travel demand keeps 3-star rates fairly firm. The FX figure is the RBA 4.00 pm reference rate for 18 Nov 2026, which appeared in search results on 19 Nov 2026.
comparable_city_reasoning: I compared Querétaro with other central Mexican colonial and business cities, mainly Guanajuato, Morelia and Puebla. Querétaro is usually a little pricier than those for dining and hotels because of its strong industrial and business economy, but cheaper than San Miguel de Allende and the main tourist areas of Mexico City.
